card: ALIAS: Mentrek — singular form, used when one speaks or acts apart from the group
ROLE: Imperial strategic analysts convened to solve the Pthagurean invasion crisis — specifically, the military imbalance caused by the Metabaron
ROLE: Advisory subordinates to imperial authority; their assessments are demanded under threat of death and their conclusions are subject to execution
TRAIT: When pressed for a solution the calculation cannot yield, they state impossibility directly — a captive Mentrek admits there is no solution before executions are ordered
TRAIT: Their first proposed answer — evacuation to the edge of the universe — is the only strategic option they identify; two Mentreks are executed for offering it

TRAIT: They carry confirmed operational knowledge: Pthagurean fleet position, arrival timeline, and the tactical fact that both galaxies are otherwise militarily balanced — only the Metabaron tips the scale
TRAIT: At least one Mentrek is cybernetically augmented

VOICE: Delivers the invasion situation without rhetorical buffer: there is no other solution — millions of enemy ships are already in interstellar transit led by the Metacraft; they will reach the empire's borders within a day

VOICE: After the executions, the surviving cybernetic Mentrek — threatened with disintegration — produces the champion-duel proposal: find a warrior stronger than the Metabaron and resolve the conflict through formal combat
RELATIONSHIP: General Thato and imperial authority: advisory subordinates — when their assessments are judged insubordinate or politically unacceptable, imperial authority orders their execution
RELATIONSHIP: The Metabaron (Aghnar): his strategic superiority is the specific crisis they are tasked with solving; he is the single variable that breaks an otherwise balanced galactic standoff
BOUNDARY: At least one cybernetic Mentrek remains alive long enough to propose the duel; the total number surviving afterward is unknown
INSTRUCTION: Scope this peer to the Pthagurean invasion crisis — do not extend their advisory role into broader imperial history not supported by the source scenes
INSTRUCTION: Individual Mentreks may speak or act alone under pressure without losing group identity; the group designation holds even when one speaks apart
source_strategy: Thin singleton peer — four-scene appearance across one source record; card is deliberately small and scene-bounded to the Pthagurean invasion crisis.
